EXAMPLE 1
Water has a large specific heat capacity. Because
of this, during day time, seawater gets heated up slowly, and becomes less warm than the
land surface near the sea. Therefore, the air molecules in contact with land become
comparatively hotterand lighter. The lighter air molecules move upward. The vacant space
above the land surface is filled by the comparatively cold and heavier air molecules coming
from the sea surface. As a result, a large mass of air moves towards the sea-shore from sea.
This is called sea breeze. During nighttime, a similar process takes place but in the opposite
direction, and air mass moves towards the sea surface from the sea-shore. The process is
called land breeze.
c) Ocean Currents:
In the ocean which extends from the pole even up to the equator, water gets heated more at
the equator than at the poles. The water level rises at the equator due to a decrease in density.
This water flows towards the poles. A current of water is set up which is known as hot
current or gulfstream. At the mean time, the cold water moves to the opposite direction
beneath the surface which is called undercurrent.

Explain this statement. 12.7 Radiation The heating of the Earth by the Sun and the transmission of heat around the fire are examples of transfer of heat by radiation. The heating of a room with an open-hearth fireplace is another example. The heat radiated by the flames, coals, and hot bricks are examples of transfer of heat by radiation. The radiation takes place even in a vacuum. Radiation does not heat the medium through which heat passes. Hence the radiation is the process of transmission of heat from one point to another without need of any material medium. During radiation, heat is transferred in the form electromagnetic wave and travel with speed of 3108 ms-1 in vacuum. Heat energy radiated by an object is called radiant energy or thermal radiation. Radiation stands for heat energy as well as for the process of transfer of heat. Thermal Radiation All objects can radiate energy continuously in the form of electromagnetic radiations at all temperature above zero kelvin. This form of energy by virtue of temperature is called thermal radiation. Thermal radiation exhibits the phenomena like reflection, refraction, interference, polarization and diffraction. Wavelength and energy of thermal radiation depend upon temperature and nature of the radiating body. Thermal radiation belongs to infrared region of electromagnetic spectrum. White clothes are preferred in summer but black clothes are preferred in winter.
